title: China-to-Philippines Industrial Motor Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Philippines IE Class Basis under PNS/IEC 60034
rows.target_requirement: The Philippines uses Philippine National Standards issued by BPS, including PNS/IEC 60034 adoption for rotating electrical machines and IE efficiency class terminology. For covered three-phase industrial AC motors, DOE energy-efficiency rules use the IEC IE class framework and set IE2 as the minimum for in-scope categories.
target_standards: PNS/IEC 60034 series for rotating electrical machines
Philippines DOE energy efficiency rules for covered motors
BPS Philippine National Standards programme
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly uses GB 18613 for motor IE efficiency classes aligned with IEC 60034-30-1, GB 12665 for cooling-related requirements, and CCC as a baseline for low-voltage motors when the model falls inside the CCC catalogue scope.
china_standards: CCC catalogue requirements for motors under 1 kV where applicable
rows.gap: The IE class names may align, but Philippines acceptance depends on DOE and BPS/DTI evidence under PNS/IEC 60034 and local certification rules. A China GB 18613 statement alone does not replace Philippines documentation, PS Mark, or ICC requirements.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for covered motors under DOE energy-efficiency rules and BPS/DTI market-access controls
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory where GB 18613 and applicable CCC scope apply in China

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat PNS/IEC 60034 and DOE/BPS acceptance as the Philippines basis; do not assume China GB 18613 or CCC documents alone are enough for Philippines market access.

source.publisher: Bureau of Philippine Standards (BPS), Department of Trade and Industry

rows.requirement: 60 Hz Rated Design for the Philippines Grid
rows.target_requirement: The Philippines is a 60 Hz market with common 380/220 V three-phase supply. Industrial motors should be designed, rated, nameplated, and tested for the intended 60 Hz duty. The nominal three-phase voltage may look familiar to China exporters, but the frequency mismatch is critical.
target_standards: PNS/IEC 60034 series for rated performance and marking
Philippines 380/220 V three-phase, 60 Hz grid practice
rows.china_equivalent: China domestic industrial motors are commonly rated for 380 V, 50 Hz service. Some export models may have dual-frequency or 60 Hz ratings, but this must be supported by the nameplate, design file, efficiency data, and thermal validation at 60 Hz.
china_standards: CCC catalogue requirements for motors under 1 kV where applicable
rows.gap: This is the critical Philippines gap: a China 50 Hz motor is not directly compatible with a Philippines 60 Hz installation. Speed, torque, current, heating, efficiency, noise, vibration, and lifetime claims can change and must be revalidated for 60 Hz service.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory practical requirement for Philippines installation and PNS/IEC 60034 evidence at 60 Hz
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory only to the declared China-market rating and applicable China rules

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] A China 50 Hz rating is a red flag for the Philippines. Require a true 60 Hz rating, nameplate, efficiency test basis, and thermal validation before treating the motor as Philippines-ready.

source.publisher: Department of Energy, Republic of the Philippines

rows.requirement: DOE MEPS for Covered Three-Phase Industrial Motors
rows.target_requirement: Philippines DOE energy-efficiency rules apply to covered three-phase industrial AC motors, including the common 0.75-375 kW scope, and require at least IE2 for in-scope categories. Evidence should be based on the applicable PNS/IEC 60034 efficiency framework and local DOE requirements.
target_standards: Philippines DOE Department Circular on energy efficiency for motors
PNS/IEC 60034-30-1 IE class framework
PNS/IEC 60034-2-1 efficiency test framework
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly uses GB 18613 for IE efficiency classes aligned with IEC 60034-30-1, plus GB 12665 for cooling-related requirements and CCC for low-voltage motors where the CCC catalogue applies.
china_standards: CCC catalogue requirements for motors under 1 kV where applicable
rows.gap: China GB 18613 evidence may show an IE class, but it does not automatically satisfy DOE Philippines paperwork, model registration, or market surveillance expectations. The motor must be evaluated against the Philippines scope and 60 Hz rating.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — IE2 minimum for in-scope motors under DOE energy-efficiency rules
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory where GB 18613 applies in China

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Confirm the model is within DOE motor scope and demonstrate IE2 or better using Philippines-accepted evidence at the declared 60 Hz rating.

source.publisher: Department of Energy, Republic of the Philippines

rows.target_requirement: For Philippines use, motor efficiency should be declared and supported for 60 Hz operation because the grid frequency is 60 Hz. A 50 Hz efficiency value from a China domestic rating may not represent the motor's actual Philippines operating point.
target_standards: PNS/IEC 60034-2-1 efficiency test framework
PNS/IEC 60034-30-1 IE class framework
Philippines DOE energy efficiency rules for covered motors
rows.china_equivalent: China GB 18613 declarations are often tied to 50 Hz China-market ratings. Export variants can be built for 60 Hz or dual frequency, but the rating, loss data, temperature rise, and efficiency must be documented for that export configuration.
rows.gap: The key efficiency gap is frequency, not just class. A motor that passes IE2 or IE3 at 50 Hz may have different efficiency and heating at 60 Hz. Philippines submissions should not rely on a 50 Hz-only China test report unless the authority or buyer accepts an equivalence rationale.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory practical evidence for 60 Hz Philippines use where DOE scope applies
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory to declared China rating; 60 Hz evidence required only if declared for export configuration

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not treat a China 50 Hz efficiency report as sufficient by default. Ask for 60 Hz loss, efficiency, and thermal evidence for the Philippines model.

source.publisher: Department of Energy, Republic of the Philippines

rows.requirement: DOE Labels, Declarations, and Market Surveillance
rows.target_requirement: DOE energy-efficiency compliance for covered motors may require importers or suppliers to keep test reports, declarations, product information, and model records available for inspection. Philippines market surveillance can check whether marketed motors match the declared IE class and 60 Hz performance.
target_standards: Philippines DOE energy efficiency rules
Energy Efficiency and Conservation Act implementing rules
PNS/IEC 60034 series
rows.china_equivalent: China suppliers commonly maintain GB 18613 test reports, CCC certificates where applicable, factory inspection records, and nameplate data for China domestic compliance. These records are useful inputs but are not a substitute for Philippines DOE or BPS/DTI compliance files.
china_standards: CCC catalogue requirements for motors under 1 kV where applicable
rows.gap: The exporter must map China model documents to the Philippines model, voltage, frequency, and IE claim. Changes in winding, frame, cooling, or frequency rating can make a China test report no longer representative of the imported Philippines product.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory recordkeeping and surveillance exposure for covered products
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory documentation for China domestic scope; not automatically valid for Philippines

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Build a Philippines-specific DOE compliance file that ties each imported model to 60 Hz test evidence, IE2 or better claims, and the exact nameplate configuration.

source.publisher: Department of Energy, Republic of the Philippines

rows.requirement: EMC Evidence for Motor Assemblies and Drives
rows.target_requirement: Standalone industrial motors may be assessed mainly under PNS/IEC 60034 performance and safety expectations, but motor systems sold with variable frequency drives, starters, electronic controllers, or control panels may need EMC evidence under applicable PNS/IEC or IEC-based product standards and buyer specifications.
target_standards: PNS/IEC 60034 series
Applicable IEC-based EMC standards for drives or electronic controllers
BPS/DTI product standards where included in mandatory scope
rows.china_equivalent: China motor documentation commonly includes GB 18613 efficiency evidence, GB 12665 cooling evidence, CCC where applicable, and sometimes GB/T or IEC EMC reports for drives or control equipment. These reports should be checked against the exact Philippines system configuration.
china_standards: CCC catalogue requirements for motors under 1 kV where applicable
rows.gap: A bare motor and a motor-plus-drive package can have different Philippines compliance expectations. China EMC reports for a drive or panel may not cover the exported combination, cable lengths, filters, enclosure, or 60 Hz operating configuration.

mandatory_status.target: Conditional — depends on whether electronics, drives, panels, or buyer-mandated EMC standards are included
mandatory_status.cn: Conditional — CCC and EMC evidence depend on product configuration and China catalogue scope

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Confirm whether the exported item is a bare motor or an electronic motor system; EMC evidence should match the exact Philippines configuration and not just a China domestic component report.

source.publisher: Bureau of Philippine Standards (BPS), Department of Trade and Industry

rows.requirement: NTC Approval for Radio-Enabled Motor Equipment
rows.target_requirement: If the motor, drive, controller, gateway, sensor, or monitoring module includes Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular, LoRa, RFID, or other radio transmission, the radio module or finished equipment may need approval from the National Telecommunications Commission before import or sale.
target_standards: National Telecommunications Commission equipment approval rules
Philippines radio equipment type approval requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China radio-enabled control modules may hold SRRC or CCC-related approvals for China, while the motor itself may rely on GB 18613, GB 12665, and CCC where applicable. China radio approvals do not replace Philippines NTC approval.
china_standards: SRRC radio approval where applicable in China
CCC catalogue requirements for motors under 1 kV where applicable
rows.gap: The gap appears when a motor product becomes connected equipment. Even if the motor and drive satisfy PNS/IEC or DOE requirements, an embedded radio module can create a separate NTC approval path before Philippines import or sale.

mandatory_status.target: Conditional — mandatory when radio transmitters are included
mandatory_status.cn: Conditional — China radio and CCC approvals depend on product configuration

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Screen industrial motors for wireless modules. If any radio function is present, add an NTC approval check alongside BPS/DTI and DOE compliance.

source.publisher: National Telecommunications Commission, Republic of the Philippines

rows.requirement: BPS/DTI PS Mark for Covered Electrical Products
rows.target_requirement: BPS under DTI issues Philippine National Standards and operates mandatory product certification for covered products. Covered electrical products may require the Philippine Standard Quality Mark before local sale, supported by product testing, factory assessment, and conformity evidence against applicable PNS.
target_standards: BPS mandatory product certification scheme
Philippine Standard Quality Mark
Applicable PNS for covered electrical products
rows.china_equivalent: China suppliers may have CCC certificates for low-voltage motors in CCC scope, GB 18613 efficiency evidence, and GB 12665 cooling evidence. These are useful inputs for a technical file but do not replace the Philippines PS Mark route.
china_standards: CCC catalogue requirements for motors under 1 kV where applicable
rows.gap: A China CCC certificate is not a Philippines PS Mark. Importers must confirm whether the motor model is on the BPS mandatory list and, if covered, obtain the local certification route before sale.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory when the product is covered by BPS mandatory certification
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory where CCC and China standards apply in China

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Check BPS coverage early. If the motor is covered, plan for PS Mark certification rather than relying on China CCC or GB reports alone.

source.publisher: Bureau of Philippine Standards (BPS), Department of Trade and Industry

rows.requirement: Import Commodity Clearance for Non-PS Certified Imports
rows.target_requirement: For imported covered products that do not already carry the PS Mark, BPS/DTI may require Import Commodity Clearance before release or distribution. ICC review can require shipment documents, test reports, product identification, and evidence against applicable PNS requirements.
target_standards: BPS Import Commodity Clearance scheme
DTI product certification rules
Applicable PNS for imported covered electrical products
rows.china_equivalent: China export packs commonly contain invoices, packing lists, certificates of origin, factory test reports, GB 18613 evidence, and CCC certificates where applicable. These documents must be supplemented with Philippines ICC-specific documentation and local importer filings.
china_standards: CCC catalogue requirements for motors under 1 kV where applicable
rows.gap: The import gap is procedural and can block customs release or distribution. A shipment of China motors without PS Mark or ICC planning may be delayed even if the underlying technical design is acceptable.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for covered imports without applicable PS certification
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory China export documents do not replace Philippines ICC

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] For covered imported motors, decide before shipment whether the route is PS Mark certification or ICC. Do not ship on China documents alone.

source.publisher: Bureau of Philippine Standards (BPS), Department of Trade and Industry

rows.requirement: Importer Responsibility and Product Identity Control
rows.target_requirement: Philippines importers and distributors are responsible for ensuring that imported motors match the certified or cleared model, rating, brand, nameplate, frequency, voltage, and technical file. Product identity matters because 50 Hz and 60 Hz variants of the same frame or model family may not be equivalent.
target_standards: BPS/DTI market surveillance and product certification rules
DOE energy-efficiency compliance rules
PNS/IEC 60034 marking and rating expectations
rows.china_equivalent: China factories often maintain model families with domestic 50 Hz variants and export 60 Hz variants. GB 18613, GB 12665, and CCC evidence must be mapped carefully to the exact exported model, not merely to a similar China domestic product family.
china_standards: CCC catalogue requirements for motors under 1 kV where applicable
rows.gap: The risk is model substitution: a certified 60 Hz export model and a cheaper China 50 Hz domestic model may look similar but are not the same compliance article. Import records, labels, certificates, and test reports should identify the exact Philippines variant.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory practical obligation under certification, import clearance, and market surveillance
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory only to China domestic certification scope unless exported variant is separately documented

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Lock the exact 60 Hz Philippines model identity before certification and shipment. Avoid treating a similar China 50 Hz model as interchangeable.

source.publisher: Department of Trade and Industry, Republic of the Philippines

rows.requirement: Electrical and Mechanical Safety under PNS/IEC 60034
rows.target_requirement: Industrial motors for the Philippines should meet applicable PNS/IEC 60034 requirements for rating, marking, temperature rise, insulation, duty, protection, and performance. Covered electrical products may also need BPS/DTI certification evidence before sale.
target_standards: PNS/IEC 60034 series
BPS mandatory product certification where applicable
DTI product safety and market surveillance rules
rows.china_equivalent: China motor safety and performance files commonly include GB 18613 efficiency evidence, GB 12665 cooling requirements, factory routine tests, and CCC certificates for low-voltage motors in CCC scope. These do not automatically demonstrate PNS/IEC 60034 conformity for the Philippines variant.
china_standards: CCC catalogue requirements for motors under 1 kV where applicable
rows.gap: The Philippines safety file must reflect the actual 60 Hz product. Temperature rise, insulation stress, fan cooling, speed, bearings, and enclosure performance can differ from a China 50 Hz version.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for applicable PNS/IEC 60034 conformity and BPS/DTI covered product controls
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory where China standards and CCC scope apply

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Build the Philippines safety file around the 60 Hz variant and applicable PNS/IEC 60034 clauses; China domestic CCC or GB files are not enough by themselves.

source.publisher: Bureau of Philippine Standards (BPS), Department of Trade and Industry

rows.target_requirement: Philippines-ready industrial motors should clearly mark voltage, frequency, phase, output, duty, speed, insulation class, enclosure or IP rating, efficiency class, and certification or clearance markings where applicable. The marking must support 380/220 V three-phase, 60 Hz use when that is the intended supply.
target_standards: PNS/IEC 60034 marking requirements
BPS/DTI certification or ICC marking requirements where applicable
DOE energy-efficiency information requirements for covered motors
rows.china_equivalent: China-market nameplates commonly show 380 V, 50 Hz, GB standard references, factory serials, and CCC marking where applicable. Export nameplates should not simply reuse China domestic 50 Hz markings when the Philippines product is intended for 60 Hz service.
china_standards: CCC catalogue requirements for motors under 1 kV where applicable
rows.gap: A misleading or incomplete nameplate can create both safety and customs problems. The most important check is that the plate and manual do not present a 50 Hz-only China product as suitable for the Philippines 60 Hz grid.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for PNS/IEC 60034 marking, DOE information, and BPS/DTI clearance where applicable
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for China domestic marking; export marking must match the Philippines configuration

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Review the nameplate before shipment. A Philippines motor should state the correct 60 Hz rating and certification or clearance identifiers where required.

source.publisher: Department of Trade and Industry, Republic of the Philippines
